subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for agents, and if so should it be modeled as tools.selfDeny, delegateOnly, scoped allow entries, or folded into the per-spawn toolsAllow design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes a public config surface and security boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent semantics or naming.

options.title: Add explicit delegate-only policy
options.body: Introduce an optional per-agent policy that removes tools from the requester's own model surface while preserving deny-wins and allowing audited subagent inheritance.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let the per-spawn toolsAllow work handle child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still needs separate profiles or instructions.

options.title: Keep monotonic inheritance
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation and document the security rationale plus separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Add explicit delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Introduce an optional per-agent policy that removes tools from the requester's own model surface while preserving deny-wins and allowing audited subagent inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Current code history points to Vincent Koc on the relevant resolver/config paths, making him the best available owner for the concrete API and implementation direction.
